definitions.explanation: A mountainous island south of Kyushu, famous for its ancient cedar forests and heavy rainfall. In 1993 it became one of Japan's first natural World Heritage sites.

examples.english: It rains a lot on Yakushima.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏休|なつやす}み→夏休み：02925_natsuyasumi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{屋久島|やくしま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{旅|たび}→旅：03407_tabi⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I traveled to Yakushima over the summer holidays.

examples.japanese: {屋久島|やくしま}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{樹齢|じゅれい}→樹齢：23245_jurei⟧{数千年|すうせんねん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧いわれる{縄文杉|じょうもんすぎ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: On Yakushima, many people hike to see the Jōmon Sugi, a cedar said to be thousands of years old.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {屋久|やく}⟦{杉|すぎ}→杉：03889_sugi⟧: Yakushima cedar (trees over about 1,000 years old)
- {縄文杉|じょうもんすぎ}: the Jōmon Sugi, the island's best-known giant cedar
- {屋久島|やくしま}⟦{登山|とざん}→登山：03457_tozan⟧: hiking on Yakushima

CULTURAL NOTE:
The island is so wet that it is said to rain "thirty-five days a month," a phrase from Hayashi Fumiko's novel {浮雲|うきぐも}. Its mossy forests are widely said to have inspired the forest in the animated film もののけ⟦{姫|ひめ}→姫：12233_hime⟧.
